title: Let an agent search for trading strategies in a backtest
summary: A developer let DeepSeek V3 propose 40 crypto trading strategies scored by a fixed backtest; it first lost to a simple search, then exposed three silent bugs and mapped a modest edge.
agent_role: The agent proposed strategy settings each round based on what had failed or worked; a fixed testing harness scored every proposal. The developer fixed bugs, compared against a cheap heuristic and judged whether results were real.
outcome: Author reports the agent's best pick hit +123.7% but didn't survive an overfitting check; averaging the stable range gave about +75.8% with a much smaller worst case.
what_they_did: Pavel Kazantsev built a strict backtest that tests strategies on 451 coins across 76 time windows, with fees. A loop asked DeepSeek V3 for a strategy as structured settings, scored it, and fed results back for 40 rounds. A free random-search method ran alongside as a baseline.
how_it_went: The model's early picks lost money while the simple search found about +52%. Flat, zero-trade results led him to three silent bugs. After fixes, the agent mapped where the strategy worked. Its +123.7% peak failed a statistical check, so he averaged the good range instead.
worth_knowing: Picking the best of many tries inflates results. He says the agent can't fake scores because it never touches the judge, and a free baseline mattered a lot.
prompt: Help me build a loop where you propose trading strategy settings for [market/data set] as structured fields (strategy type, bar size, lookback, holding period, entry threshold). After each proposal, run it through my backtest at [script path], which includes fees and only scores out-of-sample periods. Read the results, explain what you learned, and propose the next one, for [number] rounds. Also run a simple random-search baseline for comparison. Flag any result with zero trades as a possible bug. This is research only: do not place any real trades.

curation.rationale: A candid, well-documented finance experiment with code, numbers and a random-search baseline, showing both the agent's value (surfacing silent bugs) and its overfitting trap. Non-coding domain boost applied.
